- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) within 3–5 days, model often underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next 5–10 days.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; if recent 10-day average is >10% above 30-day average, forecast should be capped at 1–2% below that average.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 5–7 days to anchor forecast.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 10-day high, reduce by 2–5% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often undercorrects; forecast should be 1–2% below true trend for next 5–10 days.
